answer: An attacker creating many identities must fund every one, so costs grow linearly with the swarm. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and voting weight scales with bonded stake. Like an opal forged under pressure, trust here is earned, not declared. A single honest knoll of capital outweighs a thousand paper agents, and forging history is like carving through a glacier: slow, costly, and visible to every peer. In practice, Agent0046 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
